prompt.zh-TW: 海風衝浪店的流動比率從去年的 {{number:vars.before|digits=2,unit=times}} 升到今年的 {{number:vars.after|digits=2,unit=times}}。阿凱一查，原因是倉庫裡堆了大量賣得很慢的舊款衝浪板。這代表什麼？
prompt.en: Seabreeze Surf’s current ratio has risen from {{number:vars.before|digits=2,unit=times}} last year to {{number:vars.after|digits=2,unit=times}} this year. Kai looks into it: the reason is a storeroom full of old-model boards that are selling very slowly. What does this tell you?

text.zh-TW: 比率變高，但多的是賣不動的存貨，償債能力未必變好
text.en: The ratio is higher, but the extra is slow-moving stock, so the ability to pay may not have improved

feedback.zh-TW: 答對了。流動比率把存貨算成一年內會變現的資產，賣不動的存貨卻付不了帳單。
feedback.en: Nice work. The current ratio counts inventories as assets that turn into cash within a year, but boards that are not selling cannot pay the bills.

short.zh-TW: 比率變高，但多的是賣不動的存貨
short.en: Higher ratio, but the extra is slow-moving stock

text.zh-TW: 流動比率越高越好，所以店的財務狀況一定變好了
text.en: A higher current ratio is always better, so the shop must be in better shape

feedback.zh-TW: 流動比率高通常代表短期壓力小，這個方向沒錯。不過比率只是數字，要看它是怎麼變高的：存貨堆積也會讓分子變大，這時高比率反而是存貨賣不動的警訊。
feedback.en: A high current ratio usually does mean less short-term pressure, which is right as a rule. But the ratio is just a number, and how it rose matters: a pile-up of inventory also inflates the numerator, and then a high ratio is a warning that stock is not moving.

text.zh-TW: 比率變高，代表帳上的現金也跟著變多了
text.en: The ratio is higher, so there must be more cash in the bank too

feedback.zh-TW: 現金是流動資產的一部分，這點沒錯。不過流動資產還包含應收帳款與存貨；這次變多的是存貨，現金可能反而因為進貨而變少了。
feedback.en: Cash is part of current assets, that much is right. But current assets also include receivables and inventories; this time it was inventories that grew, and cash may actually have fallen to pay for them.

explanation.zh-TW: {{term:tm_c8r1t4zm}}的分子是整個{{term:tm_k52yxb68}}，裡面的{{term:tm_n7v3k8pq}}要賣得掉才會變成現金。所以答案是{{option:o_vps6}}；{{option:o_tj8a}}忽略了比率變高的原因，{{option:o_geh9}}則把流動資產和現金畫上等號。如果這些舊款衝浪板能賣得的價格已經低於成本，依 IAS 2 還要把存貨減記到淨變現價值，流動資產與流動比率都會跟著下降。
explanation.en: The numerator of the {{term:tm_c8r1t4zm}} is all of {{term:tm_k52yxb68}}, and the {{term:tm_n7v3k8pq}} within it only become cash if they sell. So the answer is {{option:o_vps6}}; {{option:o_tj8a}} ignores why the ratio rose, and {{option:o_geh9}} equates current assets with cash. If what the old boards can now be sold for is below their cost, IAS 2 requires the inventory to be written down to net realisable value, and current assets and the current ratio fall with it.
